memory_update.text: POWL should be tracked as an underfollowed engineered electrical-equipment candidate for AI data-center power delivery, especially medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power systems.
IESC should be tracked as a second-order data-center electrical systems and infrastructure-services candidate, with key evidence in segment growth, backlog, and margin contribution.
MYRG should be tracked as a lower-attention grid interconnection and transmission/substation construction candidate, but AI-specific exposure needs stronger backlog evidence.
ASPI is a speculative shadow-lane HALEU/enrichment candidate; do not promote beyond Layer 1 without technical validation, regulatory pathway clarity, financing, and binding offtake evidence.

Need a separate verification pass for transformer OEMs, switchgear suppliers, utility interconnection engineering firms, and private/public HALEU participants to distinguish durable chokepoints from project-cycle beneficiaries.

node: Grid interconnection, nuclear fuel cycle, baseload power, and data-center electricity supply
summary: Expanded the node away from obvious hyperscalers, utilities, and nuclear generators into four US-listed second-order candidates: engineered medium-voltage electrical equipment, data-center electrical systems integration, transmission/substation contracting, and speculative HALEU/enrichment optionality. The strongest near-term evidence is in electrical infrastructure suppliers and contractors tied to data-center power delivery; the nuclear-fuel shadow lane remains higher-duration and more regulatory/technical-risk dependent.
